startup.name: Ploy
startup.one_liner: Ploy turns your website into your company's growth engine
startup.description: Only a one line pitch is available: a product that makes a company website drive growth, probably AI driven optimization, personalization or content for B2B sites. Team of 14, unusually large for a batch company. No founder background or traction was provided. Batch Spring 2026.

yc_acceptance.basis: Test note: the company was accepted, so this is an if accepted view. A blind prior starts near 1 percent, and the factors in the YC acceptance table are applied loosely here. Not part of the scored test.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC might decline because the pitch is generic, the category of AI website growth tools is crowded with funded players, and there is no stated founder background or traction. A team of 14 suggests an existing business, so interviewers would need real revenue to justify a spot.

anchors.source: Ran python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry B2B --years 2022-2025 --calibration-only: seed 49 / 59 / 65 percent (lower, known, upper), series A 13 / 15 / 29 with cond 26 percent (n=74), series B cond 16 percent (n=19), series C cond 0 percent (n=3, too small). Broad cohort also checked with --industry B2B --years 2018-2021: seed cond 81, A cond 32, B cond 39, C cond 57 percent.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Near the 59 percent anchor. A 14 person team suggests an existing product and possibly revenue, which helps, but the category is crowded and the description is empty. The seed step here means a round above the standard 500K YC deal within about 12 months, and the anchor is for any seed ever, so the 12 month window pulls it down while a hot category pushes it up.

bands.rationale: Small round just above the YC check, mostly angels, if traction is thin.
Typical 2022+ B2B seed with about 3.2M median in the cohort and market seed pre money near 18M.
Hot round led by a top fund on strong credentials and a fast demo.

ladder.why_it_fails: A round above the YC check fails if the product is seen as one more AI SEO or personalization tool with weak differentiation. Investors have seen many, and analogs like rankai, maintouch and dynamite raised little or nothing. Without a metric such as revenue growth, a 14 person burn is a worry.

bands.rationale: Modest Series A at current medians near 17M raise and 60M pre, shaded down for slower sales.
Core case, 2022+ B2B cohort median Series A of about 15M.
Breakout traction earns a premium Series A in a hot category.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A fails if customers see little lift from the tool or churn once the AI search content wave fades. Webflow and HubSpot add native optimization, and budgets for personalization shrink in downturns, so only clear conversion gains fund growth. Growth tooling analogs such as mutiny, positional and rankscience show that only measured customer lift, not the pitch, moves a company to the next round.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The most likely failure is being squeezed into a feature of larger marketing platforms: growth tools are crowded, results are hard to prove and buyers consolidate vendors. An acquisition of the team or product, as with positional and zaraz, is a common soft landing. Growth tooling analogs such as mutiny, positional and rankscience show that only measured customer lift, not the pitch, moves a company to the next round.

analogs.relevance: AI website personalization for B2B, the clearest leader.
analogs.outcome_summary: Reached Series B and remains alive after pivoting toward an AI agent product.
Raised a seed and was acquired.
Alive, with only seed funding after many years.

killers.evidence: Webflow Optimize, HubSpot, Optimizely, Mutiny and many AI SEO tools overlap.
killers.mitigation: Choose a narrow B2B segment and prove lift.

killers.evidence: Public lift numbers for personalization are mostly vendor claims. according to the market research gathered for this evaluation and the analog records.
killers.mitigation: Measure pipeline attribution for each customer.

killers.risk: Large team burn without matching revenue
killers.evidence: 14 people is large for a company at batch start.
killers.mitigation: Show revenue per head and keep runway.

killers.risk: Dependence on search and AI answer engines changing rules
killers.evidence: Growth tools tied to search traffic suffer when algorithms or AI answers shift.

competition_now.name: Mutiny
competition_now.what: AI web conversion and personalization for B2B.
competition_now.traction: Most named B2B specialist, priced thousands per month.

competition_now.name: Webflow Optimize
competition_now.traction: Part of a large site builder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Running AI content, experiments and personalization on customer sites is buildable with current models and standard web tools. Hard parts are measurement, integrations and trust with customer data, which a 14 person team can handle.

takeover_risk.rationale: Website platforms already bundle optimization and add AI features monthly, and they own the customer and the site. Incentive is high because it increases retention for them.

evidence.claim: B2B teams pay thousands per month for personalization and conversion tools, with a mature vendor field.
Lift claims are mostly vendor made, so need is real but proof is weak.

actions: Publish three case studies with measured lift

roadmap.proof: 1M ARR with net retention above 100 percent

pros.point: Sizable team and likely existing product
pros.evidence: 14 people at batch start, unusual for YC.
Mutiny and others charge thousands per month for similar tools.

brand.name: Ploy
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Ploy" --era 2022+ gave invented or proper noun, 4 characters, 1 syllable.
strengths: Very short, memorable and easy to spell
weaknesses: Word ploy means a trick, a slightly manipulative connotation for marketing buyers
brand.rationale: Short names did well in older eras in the name tables, and it is easy to say. The meaning of a cunning plan may be playful for growth marketing but is not a strong driver.

narrative.headline: Unclear pitch but a large team in a crowded growth tools category, so a seed is plausible and later rounds need proof of lift.
narrative.general_summary: Ploy has only a one line pitch about turning websites into growth engines. A team of 14 hints at an existing business, which helps with a seed. The category is crowded, with specialists like mutiny and bundled features from Webflow and HubSpot, and most peers in the data stayed small or sold early. The base case is a seed or a small exit, with Series A roughly one in four to three. Description is missing, so the forecast has wide uncertainty.

assumptions: Blind test: only the YC listing text was used for the company itself.
Seed means more than 500K within about 12 months of batch start; cohort anchors are for any seed ever.
Recent batches are right censored in the base rates.
Web results dated after the batch start were ignored.
The input has no description, so the product is inferred from a one line pitch and the website field alone.
